newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Metro up as 1996 sales hit target.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Metro up as 1996 sales hit target.

text.p: German retail giant Metro AG reported on Wednesday that 1996 group sales were unchanged at 62 billion marks ($37.6 billion), and said pre-tax profits would be in line with target at between 1.0 and 1.1 billion marks.
Revenue growth was hit by the sale of over 200 grocery and consumer stores and a mail-order unit, but that was offset by the purchase of 27 Bauspar GmbH building supply outlets.
Discounting the impact of the disposals, 1996 sales grew by 2.1 percent, the company said in a statement.
"The preliminary group sales of Metro AG were within the range of our expectations," chief executive Klaus Wiegandt said.
Shares in Swiss-controlled Metro, Europe's largest retail conglomerate, have slipped since the company was created out of a merger of three German retail groups last summer.
But the stock market reacted positively to the figures, pushing Metro ordinary shares up 2.45 marks to 128.45 marks by the Frankfurt bourse close.
Trinkaus Capital Management said it was raising its rating on Metro's preference shares shares to buy for the first time from its earlier view of outperform.

Trinkaus made the recommendation on the preference shares because it believed the dividend payout of 4.25 marks per share was secure. Metro preferreds rose 2.20 marks to 92.70 in a generally stronger market.

The bank said Metro's results were in line with forecasts but said weak industry conditions prompted it to cut its 1997 earnings estimates for Metro to 8.50 marks per share from 10.75 marks and the 1998 estimate to 10 marks from 12 marks.
Trinkaus said Metro was the best-positioned retailer in Germany to deal with the tough economic climate and would enjoy "overproportional participation" in any recovery.

Metro said international sales were up a strong 10.9 percent in 1996 to 3.02 billion marks. Fourth quarter sales, at 18.75 billion marks, were up 0.3 percent on a year earlier and within expectations.
The Metro group's biggest divisions all showed slight falls Cash-and-carry turnover fell 0.8 percent to 11.38 billion marks to weak demand. On a same-store basis turnover was down by 2.2 percent.

Department stores, based on the Kaufhof chain, were also down 1.5 percent to 11.56 billion marks. Sales gains in western Germany were wiped out by tough competition in the east. Taking into account the closure of several Horten outlets, same-store sales were down 0.9 percent.
Self-service stores also posted a 0.2 percent fall to 10.71 billion marks.
But Metro's Media Markt and Saturn electronics store chains, raised sales by 17.7 percent to 7.52 billion marks.
A 58 percent fall in mail order business to 453 million marks resulted from the sale of the Wenz GmbH & Co unit to the Pforzheimer Klingel-Gruppe last year.
At the beginning of 1996, Metro also sold 66 Bolle grocery stores and 142 other consumer outlets to Spar Handels AG. Those stores generated revenue of about one billion marks in 1995.
